title: finding(plugin-charts): after objectui#7681 the renderer honours `series[].type` on a `dataKey` entry, but `ChartRendererProps`' TS union still declares it only on the `name` arm — declared < enforced
body:
Filed unassigned and ungraded by the `domain:ui` execution seat (`session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`) at 2026-09-06, while reviewing PR #8080. ⛔ This seat produces no `domain:*` or grade; triage owns routing.

Filed because PR #8080 **deliberately declined** to fix it, and declining was the right call — but a docblock note is not a tracked card.

## The gap

objectui#7681 / PR #8080 routes every series array through the one normalization layer, so `ChartDataSeries.type` (the declared per-series family override, maintainer ruling 2026-08-25 on objectui#6121) is now honoured on the internal `dataKey` binding as well as the `name` binding. That was the fix, and it is correct.

`ChartRendererProps.series` in `packages/plugin-charts/src/ChartRenderer.tsx` still declares a two-arm union where:

- the `dataKey` arm has `chartType` but **no `type`**
- the `name` arm has `type` but no `chartType`

⇒ At runtime a `dataKey`-shaped entry now accepts `type`. In TypeScript it does not. The new regression pin in `ChartRenderer.specSeries.test.tsx` has to write `as any` to express the very case the card exists to fix — which is the symptom worth reading: **a test that must escape the type system to describe supported behaviour is reporting a declaration gap.**

This is `declared < enforced` — the mirror of the more familiar direction. It is not dangerous the way `declared > enforced` is (nothing silently fails), but it is still a published surface that under-describes what it accepts, and a TS consumer cannot write the supported thing without an escape hatch.

## ⛔ Why PR #8080 correctly left it alone

Quoting the docblock that PR added:

> This TS union stays as declared … at RUNTIME `type` is honoured on a `dataKey`-shaped entry too (objectui#7681, both keys are independently optional on `ChartDataSeriesSchema`), because JSON metadata never goes through this TS type. **Widening the arm to match is a separate, public-face decision this fix does not make.**

⭐ That reasoning is right and should not be re-argued: widening the arm **enlarges a published type's accept set**, which is the mechanical boundary test for `Clause-②` and would have needed contract-review tier. Smuggling it into a bug fix would have been the wrong shape. ⛔ Whoever takes this card should expect it to be contract-review work, not a tidy.

⚠️ Note the live governance question: whether `Clause-②` is directional is itself unsettled and filed as objectstack-ai/objectstack#16349. **This card is on the uncontroversial side of that** — widening a published type's accept set triggers `Clause-②` under *either* reading. ⇒ ⛔ Do not wait on #16349 to route this one.

## The options, not chosen here

- **Widen the `dataKey` arm** with `type?: ...` so the declaration matches what the renderer accepts. Simplest, and matches `ChartDataSeriesSchema`, where both keys are independently optional.
- **Collapse the two arms** into one shape carrying both `dataKey?` and `name?`. Closer to what the schema actually says, but a larger public-face change with more consumer breakage risk.
- **Deliberately keep the union narrow** and document `type`-on-`dataKey` as metadata-only (JSON never goes through this TS type). ⚠️ Costs the TS consumer the ability to express it, and leaves the test's `as any` as the standing evidence of the gap.

⛔ This card does not choose — the accept-set direction makes it a decision, not a repair.

## Dedup

Adjacent and checked: objectui#7681 (the fix that produced this), objectui#6121 (the ruling that declared `ChartDataSeries.type`), objectui#2945 (the fast path #7681 removed), objectui#7682 (series `variant` carrying three different unions across declarations and readers — the nearest neighbour, and ⛔ a different key), objectui#7690 (the undeclared axis-config dialect). ⚠️ Bounded reading, ⛔ not an exhaustive `state=all` sweep.
